metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe-index list <data-dir> --json`: every package in the index as one row per `(group, name)` identity, paginated, optionally filtered by kind. Read by scripts and agents (PROP-044 §6.5 — a CLI `--json` report is a format plain text; `foreign_parsers = many`). Source of truth for the writer: `crates/vibe-index/src/cli/list.rs` (`Envelope`, `PackageRow`); the generated reader this schema owns lives in `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index_cli/e1/list_report/`.
Always `"list"` for this report.
The registry name the index announces (from `repomd.json`), e.g. `vibespecs`.
How many packages matched the filter — the count BEFORE pagination. `u32` in the writer; counts past 2^32 cannot occur for a catalog held in memory.

How many rows `packages` carries — at most `limit` of the matched set, counted past `offset`. `usize` in the writer; JTD (RFC 8927) stops at 32-bit integers, so `uint32` is the narrowest true claim this language can make.
The pagination offset the ask carried (`--offset`, default 0). `usize` in the writer; a page index past 2^32 has no meaning.
The page size the ask carried (`--limit`, default 50). `usize` in the writer; JTD (RFC 8927) stops at 32-bit integers, so `uint32` is the narrowest true claim this language can make.
The page of rows, sorted by `(group, name)`. Required member: a matchless or fully offset ask writes `[]`, never an absent key — the writer has no skip here.
One package of the listing — a `(group, name)` identity with the versions this build can act on, its newest usable stable, and the refusals named beside them.

The kind read from the package's versions — metadata per PROP-008 §2.3, `null` only for the (rare) package row whose every version this build refused (a zero-version usable set leaves nothing to read a kind from). The key is always present: the writer's `Option` carries no skip. A plain string, not a `package_kind` ref: the field is nullable, and the codegen pass has no shape rule for a nullable vocabulary enum (`optional_shapes.rs` refuses rather than guess) — the open vocabulary (flow, feat, stack, tool, mcp, lang, or any future kind an older reader must carry verbatim) is stated here in prose; the day the pass learns that shape, this field should return to the ref.
The package's reverse-FQDN group qualifier.
The package's bare name.
Every version of this package this build can act on, ascending. Required member: a package whose every version is refused writes `[]`, never an absent key.

The newest non-prerelease version this build can act on (`usable_latest_stable`), `null` when every usable version is a prerelease or the usable set is empty. The key is always present: the writer's `Option` carries no skip.
The description of the package's newest usable version, `null` when that version declares none. The key is always present: the writer's `Option` carries no skip.
Versions of this package this build refuses to act on — named, not hidden (PROP-044 §4.5). Absent when there are none (the writer carries `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`).

One version this build refused to act on, and why — the row every `vibe-index` answering surface carries (`crates/vibe-index/src/index/quarantine.rs`, `Unavailable`). Local to this schema family: `formats/vocabularies.json` does not (yet) carry it, and each of the six report schemas that need it declare their own copy.
The refused version's group.
The refused version's bare package name.
The refused version.

The reader capabilities of `must_understand` this build lacks, in the record's own order. Required member: a refusal always writes its list, `[]` never occurring in practice today (a row exists exactly because the list is non-empty) but lawful on the wire — the writer has no skip here.
What a person or a script does about it — the fixed two-part text `recipe_for` builds (the explanation with the PROP-044 anchor, then the `fix:` surface).
